worksheet.title: Build Bit's Stack
worksheet.subtitle: Draw the blocks to get Bit to the star
worksheet.learning_goal: I can build a short program to get Bit to the star.

parts.title: You build it
parts.text: Now YOU make the program. Draw an arrow in each empty block so Bit reaches the star ★. Use ➡ to go right and ⬅ to go left. Then run your stack from the top to check Bit lands on the star.

parts.title: Build 1 — Bit on box 1, star on box 4
Get to the star
parts.prompt: Draw an arrow in each of the 3 empty blocks so Bit goes from box 1 to the star on box 4. Then run it to check.

parts.title: Build 2 — Bit on box 4, star on box 2
Your program
parts.note: The star is to the LEFT this time.

parts.title: Go left to the star
parts.prompt: Draw an arrow in each of the 2 empty blocks so Bit goes from box 4 to the star on box 2. Then run it to check.

parts.title: Build 3 — Bit on box 1, star on box 3
You try — build it yourself
parts.prompt: Draw an arrow in each of the 2 empty blocks so Bit goes from box 1 to the star on box 3. Then run it to check.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: You wrote a program! You picked the blocks and put them in order to make Bit reach the goal. That is what coders do — then they run it to make sure it works.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Build Bit's Stack
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children compose their own short block program — choosing and ordering move blocks — to make Bit reach the star, then run it to check. This is the writing side of coding: turning a goal ('get to box 4') into an ordered set of instructions and testing it.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children plan and create a sequence of steps to reach a goal, then test and refine it.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child draws an arrow (➡ or ⬅) in each empty block.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: floor boxes 1-5 with a movable star so children can walk and test the program they built.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: for Build 1, count the boxes from Bit (1) to the star (4): that is 3 steps right, so draw ➡ ➡ ➡. Run it together to confirm box 4.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — children fill the 3 blocks with ➡. Exercise 2 — the star is to the LEFT, so the blocks are ⬅ ⬅.
3. YOU TRY: Exercise 3 — box 1 to box 3 is 2 steps right: ➡ ➡.
4. Connect: 'You wrote the program — then you ran it to check. That is exactly what coders do.'

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Most common slip: too few or too many arrows — have the child count boxes from Bit to the star first, then draw that many.
Direction check: arrows point the way Bit travels; toward the star on the right is ➡, on the left is ⬅.
Simplify: do Builds 1 and 3 only (both go right). Pre-count the boxes together.
Extend: ask for a different program that also reaches the star (e.g. ➡ ➡ ⬅ ➡ for Build 3) and run it to test — there can be more than one.
Movement option: the child calls out their arrows while a partner walks the boxes to test the program.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child fills every empty block with an arrow, lands Bit on the star for each build, and can run the stack to prove it works.
